Required Courses.Name (Portuguese): Fundamentos da Computação Paralela e Distribuída para Inteligência Artificial
Required Courses.Name (English): Fundamentals of Parallel and Distributed Computing for Artificial Intelligence
Required Courses.Course Description: Study of the computational foundations for running Artificial Intelligence applications. The Von Neumann model and its limitations, concurrency, parallelism, and distribution. Processes, threads, synchronization, and task and data parallelism. Performance and scalability metrics. Parallel architectures and distributed systems, cloud computing for AI, and parallel and distributed model training techniques. Integrative case study on split, distributed, and federated learning.
Course Content: The Von Neumann model, communication bottlenecks, and limitations for Artificial Intelligence workloads
Evolution of computing infrastructure for Artificial Intelligence
Concurrency, parallelism, and distribution: definitions and conceptual distinctions
Processes, threads, and concurrent execution in shared memory
Race conditions and basic synchronization principles
Task and data parallelism
Performance and scalability metrics: speedup, efficiency, Amdahl's and Gustafson's Laws
Flynn's taxonomy and modern parallel and distributed architectures
Fundamentals of distributed systems: distributed memory, inter-process communication, naming systems, and synchronization
Cloud computing for Artificial Intelligence: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, elasticity, scalability, and computational costs
Parallel training of Artificial Intelligence models
Distributed training of Artificial Intelligence models
Case study: Introduction to split learning, distributed learning, and federated learning

Required Courses.Course Description: Study of the epistemological foundations of science and its methods, with emphasis on the philosophy of science. Analysis of the elements of scientific research in computer science, including problem formulation, hypotheses, and experimental design. Coverage of the scientific methodology specific to artificial intelligence research, with a focus on empirical evaluation, validity, reproducibility, interpretation of experimental results, and ethics.
Course Content: Science and Scientific Demarcation: criteria for scientificity, the distinction between science, pseudoscience, and technology, and the limits of scientific knowledge.
Observation, Induction, and Theory: the role of observation in science, critique of inductivism, and the influence of theories on the production of scientific knowledge.
Scientific Progress and Paradigm Shifts: falsificationism, scientific paradigms, research programs, and methodological pluralism.
Research in Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence: the nature of research in computing, the distinction between scientific research, experimental research, and technological development.
Searching for and evaluating bibliographic sources: databases, journals, and conferences in AI.
Formulating Problems and Hypotheses: defining scientific problems, abstractions, models, hypotheses, and research objectives.
Empirical Research in Artificial Intelligence: characteristics of empirical investigation in AI and machine learning, exploratory and confirmatory studies.
Experimental Design and Evaluation in Artificial Intelligence: controlled experiments, comparison of methods, metrics, and interpretation of results.
Scientific Rigor, Validity, and Reproducibility in AI: internal and external validity, experimental bias, reproducibility, and best practices in AI research.
Empirical Evaluation and Inference in AI Systems: performance metrics, statistical tests, model comparison, and scientific interpretation of evidence.
Ethics in scientific research: plagiarism, integrity, algorithmic bias, and social responsibility.

Required Courses.Name (Portuguese): Segurança, Ética e Sociedade em Inteligência Artificial
Required Courses.Course Description: Study of the risks associated with Artificial Intelligence systems and the technical foundations underlying such risks. Analysis of catastrophic risks, malicious use, and competitive dynamics in AI development. Foundations of Artificial Intelligence relevant to safety, including machine learning, deep learning, scaling laws, and pace of development. Safety of individual agents, addressing monitoring, robustness, alignment, and emergent capabilities. Safety engineering applied to AI systems, including reliability, risk decomposition, component failures, systemic factors, and extreme events. Analysis of AI as a complex sociotechnical system.
Course Content: Overview of Catastrophic Risks from Artificial Intelligence: the main existential and systemic risks of AI, including malicious use, technological races, and organizational failures.
Foundations of Artificial Intelligence: basic concepts of AI, machine learning, and deep learning, with emphasis on scaling laws and pace of development.
Safety in Single-Agent Systems: alignment, robustness, monitoring, and safety problems in individual AI agents.
Safety Engineering: principles and methods of safety engineering applied to AI systems, including reliability and failure analysis.
Complex Systems: notions of complex systems and emergent behaviors relevant to AI safety.
Beneficial Artificial Intelligence and Machine Ethics: ethical, legal, and social foundations for developing AI systems aligned with human values.
Collective Action Problems: challenges of cooperation, conflict, and incentives in AI development and use.
Governance: AI governance structures and policies at the corporate, national, and international levels.

Required Courses.Name (Portuguese): Projeto 1: Resolução de Problemas do Mundo Real
Required Courses.Course Description: Development of extension projects aimed at identifying and solving real-world problems through the application of artificial intelligence and computing techniques. Focus on interdisciplinary work, community collaboration, and social innovation.
Course Content: Identification and definition of real-world problems in different social and economic contexts.
Gathering and analysis of stakeholder needs.
Applied research and university extension methodologies.
Planning and management of collaborative projects.
Application of artificial intelligence and computing techniques to develop solutions.
Development, implementation, and prototyping of projects.
Assessment of the social and technical impact of projects.
Documentation and presentation of results.
Teamwork and interdisciplinary communication.
Ethics, social responsibility, and sustainability in technology projects.

\textbf{Community Profile:} The course works in partnership with local communities, public agencies, schools, NGOs, community associations, and small businesses facing real challenges related to technology, management, or digital inclusion. Projects are developed collaboratively, with community participation in identifying needs, defining solutions, and evaluating results, prioritizing contexts with clear social needs and potential for impact.

\textbf{Extension Objectives:} The course aims to (i) identify and co-build technological solutions to real problems together with local communities and institutions, (ii) apply computing and artificial intelligence techniques to generate social impact and support community needs, (iii) promote digital inclusion and the democratization of knowledge by bringing the university closer to society, (iv) develop sociotechnical skills in students, such as communication, ethics, cooperation, and social responsibility, and (v) strengthen UFOP's role as an agent of social transformation through collaborative, technologically oriented projects.
